answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a living vine trained along a unique cipher trellis inside a registered tundra greenhouse. A licensed horticulturist inspects one vine weekly, logging its growth as the identity's fingerprint, and random spot-checks summon the holder to stand beside their own vine within a day. One operator cannot tend vines in two greenhouses at once, and the greenhouse fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another vine, another season of growth, another inspector visit, and twice the prior fee.
